exports_to_rus_gap.unit: EUR bn (annual average ECB rates as in trade_full.json)
exports_to_rus_gap.method: Gap = Russia FCS total imports (CIF, includes EAEU trade) minus the sum of partner-reported exports to Russia in trade_full.json (FOB). The gap is split into four parts. (1) CIF/FOB valuation: 3.5-7.5% of FCS imports (triangular, mode 5.5%). This is freight and insurance, not goods sales, and it is not allocated to countries. (2) Unrecorded transit via Kyrgyzstan: the rise since 2021 in the mirror gap between partners' reported exports to KGZ (excluding Russia and Belarus) and KGZ's own reported imports (excluding Russia), times a share reaching Russia of 0.3-0.8. (3) The same for Kazakhstan: mirror-gap rise over 2019 (KAZ 2021 imports in Comtrade are incomplete), share reaching Russia 0.25-0.75; 2022 is taken as USD 0-3bn because of KAZ data problems. Transit amounts are attributed to the ORIGIN countries that recorded the sale to the hub, split by each origin's increase in exports to that hub since 2021 (China 61-65% of KGZ, 26-56% of KAZ). The hub keeps a 5-20% margin. (4) Residual: the rest of the gap, including the structural pre-war gap of about 3% of FCS seen in 2019-2021 (partner/FCS ratio 0.908-0.935) and war-specific under-recording. It is allocated pro rata to each country's reported exports to Russia in that year, with weight 0.25 for sanctions-coalition countries (their direct exports are fully recorded) and 1.0 for others. The FCS total has 0.9% noise and the partner sum has noise equal to the root-sum-square of the country ranges. Monte Carlo with 20,000 draws; the low and high are the 5th and 95th percentiles. The country values are ADDITIONS to trade_full exports_to_RUS (the share of money flowing from Russia that partner statistics miss). Summing the country lows or highs overstates the range of the total.
exports_to_rus_gap.principle: Each amount is attributed to the country whose sellers were paid for the goods: the origin for transit via EAEU hubs, plus the hub margin. A transit-country view would instead put all of components 2-3 on KGZ/KAZ.

hong_kong.question: What Hong Kong imports from Russia, by HS chapter, and whether it is gold in transit to mainland China
hong_kong.answer: Yes, it is gold. 98-99% of Hong Kong's imports from Russia since 2023 are HS 71. Gold (HS 7108) is 63% (2023), 72% (2024), 80% (2025) and 93% (Jan-Jul 2026): about 92 t in 2025 and 113 t in Jan-Jul 2026. The rest is platinum-group metals (7110), diamonds (7102) and silver (7106). Transit to mainland China is likely for a majority but not all of it. Hong Kong sends 58-83% of its gold exports to mainland China (83% in Jan-Jul 2026), and Russia supplied 7-15% of its gold imports. If Russian gold follows the average path, about 45-65% goes to the mainland, a third stays in Hong Kong vaults (imports exceeded exports by USD 21bn in 2025), and the rest goes to Thailand, Singapore, the UK, the US and Switzerland. Comtrade cannot trace origin through re-exports, so the mainland share is inferred, not observed. China's own direct imports of gold from Russia are small (USD 0.3bn in 2023, 3.3bn in 2025), so Hong Kong is the main entry route.

2026_jan_jul.note: Comtrade monthly data for August 2026 were not yet available. trade_full's EUR 17.9bn for Jan-Aug is consistent with Jan-Jul EUR 15.0bn plus about 3.0bn in August.

share_onward_to_mainland.method: HK gold exports to CHN / HK gold imports, by year (2023 0.56, 2024 0.52, 2025 0.45, Jan-Jul 2026 0.66), widened for origin-specific routing

hong_kong.implication: Keep the figure as Hong Kong's imports from Russia: money paid by Hong Kong traders to Russian sellers. If the map should show the final buyer, move 30-85% (central 55%) to China. Do not count it twice, because China's customs records gold bought through Hong Kong as imports from Hong Kong.
